full_judgment:
Mahmudul Hoque, J: In this application under Article 102(i)(a) of the Constitution of Bangladesh this Rule Nisi has been issued at the instance of the Petitioner calling upon the Respondents to show cause as to why the judgment and order No. 22 dated 13-3-2013 passed by the learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka in Artha Jan Case No. 29 of 2011 (Annexure-'K' to the Writ Petition) now pending before the Artha Rin Adalat No.3, Dhaka should not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and/or such other or further order or orders as to this court may seem fit and proper.
2. Bare necessary facts for the disposal of this Rule is, in brief, are that the Petitioner, Agrani Bank Limited instituted Artha Rin Suit No. 652 of 2004 against the Respondent Nos. 3-6 as heirs of the borrower Mrs. Fatema Salam for recovery of the loan and the said suit was decreed on contest against the Defendants on 11-10-2009. Thereafter the Petitioner Bank as decree holder put the said decree in execution by filing Artha Execution Case No. 29 of 2011. The Judgment-Debtor Respondent Nos. 3-6 filed an application on 15-11-2012 praying for allowing the Judgment-Debtors to pay the decretal amount by four equal instalments within one year and to adjust the amount already paid to the Bank before filing of the suit. In the said application the Respondents Judgment-Debtor claimed that their predecessor obtained loan from the Bank amounting to Taka 2,73,00,000. As per Section 47 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain ("AM") the Decree Holder Bank cannot claim more than thrice of the principal amount and accordingly, the Artha Rin Adalat decreed the suit for an amount of Taka 8,19,00,000 following the provisions of Section 47. But the Decree-Holder Bank filed execution case claiming an amount of Taka 14,24,63,207.38 with upto date interest which is illegal and contrary to the provision of Section 47 of the Ain. The Judgment-Debtors also claimed that they already paid an amount of Taka 2,09,70,444 to the Bank but the said amount has not been adjusted with the decretal amount at the time of filing of the execution case. As per calculation of the Judgment-Debtors, the Decree-Holder Bank after adjustment of the said amount is entitled to get only Taka 6,09,29,556 and the Respondents by filing an application sought permission of the Adalat to pay the said amount by four instalments to the Petitioner Bank within one year. The Petitioner Bank filed written objection against the said application of the Judgment-debtor. The Artha Rin Adalat heard the application and upon hearing allowed the same and deducted Taka 2,09,70,444 from the decretal amount of Taka 8,19,00,000 and directed the Judgment Debtors to pay Taka 6,09,29,556 to the Decree Holder Bank by four equal instalments within one year by the Impugned Order dated 13-3-2013. At this stage the Decree-Holder Bank has challenged the validity and propriety of the impugned order by filing this application and obtained the present Rule and Order of Stay.
3. The Respondent Nos. 3 and 4 contested the Rule by filing Affidavit-in-Opposition denying all the material allegations made in the application contending, inter alia, that the Respondents predecessor Mrs. Fatema Salam and SM Badius Salam obtained loan from the Bank who during pendency of the Artha Rin Suit died and the Respondents were made party to the suit as heirs of the original loanee. The Artha Rin Adalat after contested hearing decreed the suit. The Respondents were always ready to pay the decretal amount to the Bank as per decree subject to adjustment of the money already paid but the decree Holder Bank without adjusting the money paid and allowing instalments to the Respondents filed execution case claiming the amount beyond the decree. The Judgment Debtor Respondents filed an application before the executing court for adjustment of the amount already paid and to allow the Judgment Debtors to make payment of the rest amount by four equal instalments within one year. The Adalat upon contested hearing allowed the application and there was no illegality. The Petitioner Bank filed this Writ Petition only to harass the Respondents. Further case of the Respondents are that their predecessor obtained the loan from the Bank amounting to Taka 2,73,00,000. The Bank is entitled to claim three times of the loan amount from the borrower as per Section 47 of the Ain and accordingly, the Artha Rin Adalat decreed the suit for Taka 8,19,00,000 out of which the Respondents made payment of Taka 2,09,70,444. After deduction of the said amount the claim of the Bank stands at Taka 6,09,29,556. The executing court allowed the Respondents to pay the aforesaid amount by four equal instalments within one year. Therefore, the executing court committed no illegality in passing the Impugned Order and, as such, the Rule is liable to be discharged.
4. Mr Shamim Khaled Ahmed with Mr Syed Hasan Zobair, the learned Advocates appearing for the Petitioner Bank submit that the executing court cannot go beyond the decree but in the instant case the executing court acted as a court of appeal sitting over the decree passed by the trial court. It is also argued that the executing court by the Impugned Order in fact revisited the judgment and decree passed by the trial court affecting the rights of the parties already settled under the decree. Mr Zobair further submits that once under the decree the trial court had adjudicated the issue relating to entitlement of the plaintiff, the grievance, if any, on the part of the Defendant Judgment Debtor as aggrieved party is available in the form of an appeal and the executing court being not entitled to go beyond the decree certainly cannot reduce any amount from the decree. But the executing court by allowing Judgment Debtors application reduced the decretal amount as prayed for and, as such, the Impugned Order is illegal and liable to be set-aside.
5. Mr Asaduzzaman with Mr Md Abbas Uddin, the learned Advocates appearing for the Respondent Nos. 3 and 4 submit that the executing court is entitled to deduct any amount paid by the Judgment Debtors during the pendency of the suit or before filing of the execution case. According to them it is not disputed that the Judgment Debtors made payment of Taka 2,09,70,444 to the Petitioner Bankbefore and after filing of the suit. The trial court considering and keeping in mind the provision of Section 47 of the Ain decreed the suit for an amount three times of the principal amount of loan. As per provision of law the amount already paid by the Defendant Judgment Debtors ought to have been adjusted with the decretal amount but the trial court at the time of passing decree did not adjust the amount already paid. It is also argued that the executing court is competent enough under Order XXI, rule I of the Code of Civil Procedure to adjust the amount already paid to the Decree Holder Bank duly certified by them. In the instant case the executing court in fact exercised that power and, as such, the executing court by adjusting the said amount with the decretal amount committed no illegality and for that reason the order passed by the executing court is not liable to be interfered with.
6. In reply to the submission of the Respondents Counsel Mr Zobair submits that the executing court, no doubt, can adjust the amount paid by the Judgment Debtors after filing and during pendency of the execution proceedings. But the executing court cannot adjust again the amount paid by the Judgment Debtors which was already adjusted before filing of the suit. It is strongly argued that the Judgment Debtors during pendency of the suit made payment of Taka 62,50,000 only which was not adjusted with the claim through inadvertence, that amount may be adjusted with the claim of the Decree Holder Bank but the executing court in place of adjusting Taka 62,50,000 most illegally adjusted Taka 2,09,70,444 as prayed for by the Judgment Debtors travelling beyond the decree and, as such, the Impugned Order is illegal and liable to be set-aside.
7. Heard the learned Advocates for the parties, perused the Application, Affidavit-in-Opposition, Supplementary Affidavit and the Annexures annexed thereto.
<u>8. In the instant, Rule the only point to be considered whether the executing court can go beyond the decree and it can adjust any amount with the decree paid before filing of the suit. It is well settled that the executing court cannot go beyond the decree nor can it question its legality (3- correctness, but there is one exception to this general Rule i.e. the executing court can adjust the amount with the decree paid by the Judgment Debtors during pendency of the execution proceeding if certified by the Decree Holder. In the present case admittedly the Judgment Debtors made payment of Taka 62,50,000 to the Decree Holder during pendency of the Suit which has not been adjusted by the Decree Holder at the time of filing of the execution proceeding. In this situation the executing court is legally entitled to adjust the aforesaid amount with the decretal amount not the amount paid before filing of the suit but the executing court adjusted and deducted the amount paid before filing of the suit along with the amount paid during pendency of the suit which the executing court cannot do. It must take the decree according to its tenor but in the instant case the executing court travelled beyond the decree and, as such, the Impugned Order passed by the executing court is not in accordance with law. Had the executing court adjusted the amount of Taka 62,50,000 with the decretal amount it would have been just and proper exercise of power vested in it but in deducting the amount as prayed for, the executing court in fact sat over the decree as an appellate court and acted in affecting the rights of the parties already settled by the decree and, as such, this court finds that the Impugned Order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat amending the decree is illegal. Accordingly, the Impugned Order No.22 dated 13-3-2013 is hereby set-aside.</u>
9. Nov in the above facts and circumstances this court is inclined to direct the executing court to adjust the actual amount paid by the Judgment Debtors after filing of the suit and during pendency of the execution proceedings with the decretal amount duly certified and admitted by the Decree-Holder Bank and after adjustment of the amount actually paid by the judgment Debtor to proceed with the execution case in accordance with law and the decree passed by the trial court. However, the Judgment Debtors and the Decree Holder Bank shall be at liberty to settle the claim under the decree amicably out of court taking recourse to the provisions contained in sections 38, 45 and 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and in that event nothing of this judgment shall debar the parties to the litigation to have the claim settled amicably.
10. With the above observations, the Rule is disposed of. However, without any order as to costs.
11. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule, is hereby recalled and stand vacated.
Communicate a copy of this judgment to the court concerned at once.
End.

full_judgment:
Let the supplementary affidavit be formed as to part of the main application.
2. This Rule was issued on an application under section 115(4) of the Code of Civil Procedure at the instance of the defendant-petitioners calling upon opposite party Nos. 1-11 to show cause as to why the impugned judgment and order dated 8-10-2015, passed by the learned District Judge, Bagerhat, in Civil Revision No. 11 of 2015 allowing revisional application and setting aside the judgment and order dated 23-3-2015, passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mongla, Bagerhat, in Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2011 allowing an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure should not be set-aside and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may deem fit and proper.
3. Relevant facts for disposal of the Rule are that opposite parties as plaintiff filed the Title Suit No. 6 of 1995 in the Court of learned Assistant Judge, Mongla, Bagerhat for partition. The suit was dismissed on 5-11-1995. Against that judgment and decree the plaintiffs preferred an appeal being No. 54 of 1996 which was allowed ex-parte and the suit was sent back on remand. Thereafter/the suit was decreed ex-parte on 3-7-2006. Against that judgment and decree defendant No. 2 Dinomoni Mondal filed Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2011 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for setting aside the ex-parte decree. That Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2011 was allowed on 23-3-2015 by the learned Assistant Judge, Mongla, Bagerhat. Against that judgment and order the plaintiffs filed revision before the learned District Judge, Bagerhat being Civil Revision No. 11 of 2015 which was allowed setting aside the judgment and order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mongla, Bagerhat.
4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the learned District Judge, Bagerhat the defendant Dinomoni Mondal being dead his heirs Mohanonda Mondal filed this revision and obtained the present Rule. After filing this revision, Mohananda Mondal died leaving two sons Dulal Mondal and Paramananda Mondal who are the present petitioners.
5. Ms. Promila Biswas, learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners submits that the summons of Title Suit No. 6 of 1995 was not served upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondal. The plaintiff of the suit obtained decree by practicing fraud upon the court by suppressing service of summons.
6. In support of her contention she cited the decisions passed in the cases of Abdur Rashid and another vs Abdul Bank and another reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162 and Sonali Bank Limited and others vs Prime Global Limited and others reported in 63 DLR (AD) 99.
7. Ms. Purabi Saha, learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties contended that summons notices of the original Title Suit No. 6 of 1995 were duly served upon the defendants. She also submits that after the death of her husband she used to live with Mohananda Mondal who was another defendant in Title Suit No. 6 of 1995. Moreover, Mohanonda Mondal filed another Title Suit No. 25 of 2009 about the disputed land and Dinomoni Mondal fully aware of the suit No. 6 of 1995. Under such circumstances the petitioner is not entitled to get relief as prayed for.
8. In support of her contention she cited the decision in the cases of Osir Liddin Mondal and others vs Azizur Rahman reported in 39 DLR 403.
9. I have heard both the sides and gone through the materials on record meticulously. Whether summons was served upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondal or not it is the vital question in this case. As per provisions of the Evidence Act, burden lies upon the plaintiff to prove that summons was duly served upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondal. Regarding this matter, the plaintiffs examined two witnesses including the plaintiff No. 4 Pijus Mondal as OPW 1 and Process Server Piar Ali as OPW 2. OPW 1 Pijus Mondal stated in his examination in-chief that summons of original suit was duly served, but in his cross-examination he stated that Dinomoni Modnal came before the process server and in presence of him Piar Ali served summons to Dinomoni Mondal and she received summons putting her signature. But, he stated in his cross-examination that Dinomoni Mondal received the summons putting her finger impression which is contradictory to his earlier statement that she received summons putting her signature. Process server Piar Ali was examined as OPW 2 who deposed that in that suit he served notice only upon Dinomoni Mondal. Notice was marked as Exhibit 'ka' but in his cross-examination he stated that he has served summons upon the defendant No. 9 Nilima only and he did not serve any summons to anybody except Nilima. Admittedly there is no defendant namely Nilima in the original partition suit. Under such circumstances the learned Assistant Judge, Mongla, Bagerhat decided that notice was not duly served upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondal and accordingly, he allowed the Miscellaneous Case No. No. 4 of 2011 filed under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
10. From the judgment passed by the learned District Judge, Bagerhat it appears that he has set-aside the judgment and order passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mongla, Bagerhat by a long judgment without giving reasonable grounds. He did not consider whether the process or summons was_ duly served upon the defendant No. 1 or not. The learned District Judge, Bagerhat decided that summons was duly served upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondal since after the demise of her husband she was residing in the house of Mohananda Mondal who was plaintiff No. 1 in the original suit for which summons to be considered as duly served under Order V, rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure. But there is no material on record from which it can be ascertained that the summons in the name of Dinomoni Mondal was received by Mohananda Mondal on behalf of Dinomoni Mondal and at the time of service of summons she was residing in the house of Mohananda Mondal.
11. The learned District Judge stated in his judgment that Nilima was not a defendant in the original suit and the process server OPW 2 Piar All wrongly said in his cross-examination that defendant No. 9 was Nilima and he served summons only in the name of Nilima. Whenever it came to the knowledge of the learned District Judge that Nilima was not a defendant and the process server stated in his cross-examination that he served summons only in the name of Nilima, then he should have taken decision that service of summons upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondal was not proved. Inspite of that he decided wrongly that summons was served duly upon Dinomoni Mondal. The learned District Judge did not consider that the OPW 1 Pijus Mondal did not state a single sentence in this chief that summons of the original suit was served upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondol. Even he did not consider that the OPW-1 in his cross made contradictory statements as to receiving of summons by the defendant Dinomoni Mondal since he firstly stated that Dinomoni Mondal received the summons putting her signature and later he stated that she put her finger impression at the time of receiving summons.
12. It is transpired from the materials on record that the opposite parties failed to prove that the summons of the original suit was duly served upon the defendant-petitioner Dinomoni Mondal. The learned Assistant Judge rightly decided that the summons upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondal was not duly served.
13. Hon'ble Apex Court held in the case of Abdul Rashid and another vs Abdul Barik and another reported in 35 DLR (AD) 162 that under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code, if summons is not duly served on the defendant, that is a good ground for setting aside an ex-parte decree. In such a case question of knowledge is not at all relevant and ex-parte decree will be set-aside even if the defendant had knowledge of institution of a suit. No provision of law could be pointed out by the learned Counsel for the respondent, which dispense with the necessity of proper service of summons.
<u>14. In the case of Regent Ken International Ltd. vs Amanat Shah Ship Breaking Industries Ltd. reported in 57 DLR 234 (para-7) their Lordships held that if a party satisfies a Court that summons was not duly served upon him, the Court is bound to set-aside the ex-parte decree. In such a case, question of knowledge is not at all relevant and ex-parte decree will be set-aside even if the defendant had knowledge of institution of the suit. In the facts of the instant case, it is proved that the petitioner Dinomoni Mondal was not served with notices of the original suit and that was the cause for her non appearance when the suit was called on for hearing.</u>
<u>15. In the light of above deliberation, it is decided that the learned District Judge, Bagerhat wrongly decided that summons was served duly upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondal and, as such, he committed an error of law resulting an error in his decision occasioning failure of justice. So, the learned Assistant Judge, Mongla, Bagerhat- rightly decided that the summons was not duly served upon the defendant Dinomoni Mondal and he rightly restored the original suit in its original file and number. In fact, the plaintiff-opposite parties obtained judgment and decree in the original suit fraudulently by suppressing summons. It is settle principle of law that fraud vitiates everything. So, the judgment and decree passed in the original suit is not sustainable.</u>
16. Considering everything I find merit in the Rule. As such the Rule should be made absolute.
17. In the result, the Rule is hereby made absolute without any order as to cost.
18. The impugned judgment and order dated 8-10-2015, passed by the learned District Judge, Bagerhat, in Civil Revision No. 11 of 2015 is hereby set-aside and the judgment and order dated 23-3-2015, passed by the learned Assistant Judge, Mongla, Bagerhat, in Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2011 allowing the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure is hereby restored.
19. The order of stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated.
20. The ex-parte decree passed in Title Suit No. 6 of 1995 is hereby set-aside. The trial court is hereby directed to dispose of the suit expeditiously without unnecessary delay.
Copy of this judgment be sent to the concerned court at once.
End.

full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan, J: This civil appeal by leave granting order dated 10-5-2015 in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2565 of 2012 is directed against the judgment and decree dated 5-3-2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5297 of 2000 making the Rule absolute reversing the judgment and decree dated 7-8-2000 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Feni in Title Appeal No.41 of 1998 allowing the appeal upon reversing the judgment and decree dated 30-3-1998 passed by the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Feni Sadar in Title Suit No.50 of 1996 decreeing the suit.
2. The relevant facts necessary for the disposal of this civil appeal are, in a nutshell, that the respondents No.1 and 2 as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.50 of 1996 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Feni Sadar, Feni against the appellant and the respondents No.3-5 as defendants for permanent injunction in respect of the schedule land as appended to the plaint. The plaintiffs' case, in short, is that the predecessor of the plaintiffs Mukunda Lal Das took yearly lease of the suit land measuring 25 decimals in the year 1973-74 which was renewed from time to time and ultimately he took permanent lease of the suit land for 15 years with effect from 1st Baishak, 1388 BS to 30th Chaitra, 1403 BS in SO file No.78(XII) of 1980-1981 by registered deed dated 10-7-1981. Later on, Khatian No.172 was prepared in the name of Mukunda Lal Das and he was in possession of the suit land by preparing trace map. Although the suit land was recorded as nal, it was in fact the east bank of Gazi Ganu Dighi near to Gazi Ganu Ashram. The defendant No.1 purchased 11 decimals in plot No.1543 of Gazi Ganu Dighi from a co-sharer and 1decimal from plot No.1542 behind the back of the plaintiffs and applied for settlement of 30 decimals land including 25 decimals of plaintiff of plots No.617 and 619, but the said application was rejected on 23-12-1995 by the defendant No.2 and subsequently affirmed by the Deputy Commissioner on 3-9-1996. After rejection of settlement application, the defendant No.1 tried to encroach on the settled land of the plaintiffs plot No.617 which is East-North part of the East bank of the Dighi for which the plaintiffs' father prayed to the defendant No.3 to re-fix the area, who by opening file No.8(XI1)96 asked Magistrate Zahedul Islam to submit a report and subsequently he submitted a collusive and biased report on 25-5-1996 without any inquiry and actual physical measurement and without any notice to the plaintiffs. On the basis of the said report prepared and submitted by the learned Magistrate the defendant No.1 forcibly has been threatening to dispossess the plaintiffs from the northern part of some land of plot No.617. If the plaintiffs are dispossessed from their land which they got by settlement, they will suffer irreparable loss and injury, hence the suit.
3. The appellant as defendant No.1 contested the said suit by filing written statement, contending, inter alia, the land of plots No.617 and 619 was Khas land of the government. The total land of plot No.617 is 38 decimals while the total land of plot No.619 is 208 decimals. The predecessor of the plaintiffs Mukunda Lal Das was given settlement of 12 decimals land of plot No.617 situated on the south side of the plot and 13 decimal lands of plot No.619 situated on the north side of the plot by Nothi No.78(XIII). The rest land measuring 26 decimals of plot No.617 was vacant. The defendant No.1 acquired 12 decimal lands of plots No.1542 and 1543 adjacent to plot No.617. The defendant No.1 was in possession of 12 decimals land on the northern side of plot No.617. When the defendant No.1 was in possession of the said 12 decimals land, plaintiffs' father applied to re-fix the areas of 25 decimals settled land and Miscellaneous Case No.8(XIII) was started in the office of the defendant No.3 and by order dated 5-5-1966 it was found that the land possessed by the defendant No.1 is not settled land of plaintiffs' father. Thereafter, in pursuance to direction by the authority a team headed by Magistrate Zahedul Islam after due enquiry submitted report and as per report it was found that the defendant No.1 did not possess the settled land of plaintiffs. The defendant No.1 did not claim the land of plot No.619 and did not threaten the plaintiffs to dispossess, hence the suit is liable to be dismissed.
4. During the trial of the case three issues were framed by the trial Court. The plaintiff examined four witnesses as PWsI-4 while the defendant No.1 examined three witnesses as DWs 1-3 and the defendants No.2-4 examined one witness. The plaintiff filed the documents which had been marked as Exhibits 1-5, on the other hand, those filed by the defendant No.1 had been marked as Exhibits-A series and B series.
5. The trial Court on completion of the trial decreed the suit by judgment and decree dated 30-3-1998. Being aggrieved by the judgment of the trial Court the defendant No.1 preferred Title Appeal No.41 of 1998 and on transfer the said appeal was heard by the learned Additional District Judge, Feni and it was allowed by his judgment and decree dated 7-8-2000 reversing the judgment of the trial Court. Thereafter, the plaintiffs-respondents No.I-2 filed Civil Revision No.5297 of 2000 before the High Court Division against the judgment and decree dated 7-8-2000 passed by the appellate Court and Rule was issued. Upon final hearing the High Court Division was pleased to make the Rule absolute by judgment and decree dated 5-3-2012.
6. Being disgruntled with the judgment and decree dated 5-3-2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5297 of 2000 the defendant No.1-appellant preferred Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.2565 of 2012 before this Division and hence the instant appeal.
7. Leave was granted to consider the following grounds:
(I)	Because the High Court Division ought to have reassessed the evidence on record and expressed its satisfaction that the lower appellate Court has failed to consider the materials evidence in reversing the findings of fact arrived at by the trial Court, but the High Court Division, without reassessing the evidence on record and without giving independent findings reversed the judgment of the lower appellate Court and therefore the High Court Division committed error of law in making the Rule absolute as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside.
(II)	 Because the High Court Division reversed the judgment of the lower appellate court without reversing the material findings of the lower appellate court to the effect that the defendant is in possession of the suit land and the plaintiff has not filed the suit for cancellation of trace map prepared by the executive authority as such, the impugned judgment and order is not a proper judgment of reversal and the High Court Division committed error of law in passing impugned judgment and order as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside.
(III)	Because the High Court Division committed error of law in passing the judgment to the effect that "It also appears from the record that the defendant No.1 has already sold out his land to one Alauddin Bhuiyan on 23-10-2007 and for that reason, he lost interest to contest the suit." wherein the said fact is beyond the pleadings and neither the said deed of transfer was filed and exhibited by any parties to the suit nor the same is available in record and as such, the High Court Division has passed such finding on mere surmise and conjecture as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside.
8. Mr SM Khalequzzaman, Advocate along with Mr Md Robiul Karim, Advocate appearing on behalf of the appellant took us through the judgment and decree of the High Court Division dated 5-3-2012 passed in Civil Revision No.5297 of 2000, judgment and decree of the trial Court as well as appellate Court, the other materials on record and contended that the High Court Division has committed illegality in totally misconceiving the case of the appellant upon misreading and misconstruing the evidence and materials on record and thereby misdirected beyond the law and facts of the case in passing the erroneous judgment making the Rule absolute occasioning serious miscarriage of justice and, as such, the impugned judgment and decree is liable to be set-aside. The learned Counsel for the appellant contend further that the High Court Division ought to have reassessed the evidence on record and expressed its satisfaction that the lower appellate Court has failed to consider the materials and evidence on record in reversing the findings of facts arrived at by the trial court, but the High Court Division, without reassessing the evidence on record and without giving independent findings reversed the judgment of the lower appellate court and therefore the High Court Division committed error of aw in making the Rule absolute as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be set-aside.
9. Per contra, Mr Mohammad Mostafa, learned Advocate has opposed the arguments adduced on behalf of the appellant. The learned Counsel contend that the trial Court on proper assessment of the evidence on record decreed the suit, but the appellate Court wrongly reversed the judgment of the trial Court and thereafter the High Court Division correctly reversed the judgment and decree of the appellate Court and, as such, the judgment of the High Court Division cannot be interfered with and hence the instant appeal is liable to be dismissed.
10. We have perused the judgment and decree dated 5-3-2012 passed in Civil Revision No.5297 of 2000. We have also considered the submissions of the learned Counsels for both sides and gone through the judgment and decree of the appellate Court as well as the trial Court, evidences and other materials on record.
<u>11. On going through the impugned judgment and decree it appears that the High Court Division reversed the judgment and decree of the appellate Court without controverting the findings and observation made by the appellate Court. It is settled law that the appellate Court is the last Court of facts and in revisional jurisdiction the High Court Division can only exercise its power if there is misreading and non-reading of evidence occasioning failure of justice. But the High Court Division while passing the impugned judgment could not show any lawful ground for its interference with the judgment of the appellate Court. The High Court Division disposed of the revisional application in a very slipshod manner without discussing the case on merit. In view of the aforesaid reasons, the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division warrants interference by this Division. Therefore, we find merit in the submissions of the learned Counsels for the appellant. Moreover, the ends of justice will be met if the Civil Revision No.5297 of 2000 is heard again and disposed of on merit detailing the case of all parties. In the prevailing circumstances the impugned judgment and decree of the High Court Division cannot stand at all in the eye of law.</u>
12. The instant civil appeal is disposed of in the light of the observations made above.
13. The judgment and decree dated 5-3-2012 passed by the High Court Division in Civil Revision No.5297 of 2000 is set-aside. The single Bench of the High Court Division presided over by Ms Fatema Najib, J. is directed to hear the matter afresh and dispose of the same preferably within 6(six) months from the date of receipt a copy of this judgment and order.
End.

full_judgment:
M Enayetur Rahim, J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgment and order dated 31-8-2016 passed by the High Court Division Civil Revision No. 3441 of 2010 making the Rule absolute.
2. The facts, relevant for disposal of the appeal, are that the present respondents instituted Title Suit No. 42 of 2003 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Kotalipara, Gopalgonj, impleading the defendants-appellant herein and others praying for a declaration that the judgment and decree dated 27-5-2003 obtained by the defendant in Title Suit No. 06 of 2003 (decree signed on 1-6-2003) is collusive, illegal and not binding upon the plaintiffs. In the plaint it is contended that while Annada Charan Saha, Kanjiram Saha, Jotnamoyee Saha, Narayan Chandra Sana, Rakhal Chandra Saha, Hare Krishna Saha, Mohendra Kumar Saha and Amullay Kumar Saha along with their other co-sharers were possessing the suit land as being lawful owners RS Khatian Nos. 155, 27 and 40 and SA Khatian Nos. 134, 27 and 40 were correctly prepared in their names. Mohendra Kumar Saha died leaving behind his son Ranjan Kumar Saha who became the owner of 1.27 acre of land appertaining to Mouza-Unsia, who transferred the entire 1.27 acre of land in SA khatian No. 27, plot No. 451 and 452, SA Khatian No. 134, Plot Nos. 84 and 85 and in khatian No. 40 Plot No. 451 of No. 66 Amtoli Mouza to one Jogesh Chandra Dhupi vide deed No. 4595 dated 3-5-0975 and deed No.5193 dated 6-6-1975. Jogesh Chandra Dhupi thereafter transferred the said 1.27 acre of land to the plaintiff-respondent No. 1 vide deed No. 3449 dated 16-8-1982 and since then the plaintiff has been enjoying the same upon constructing house and planting trees. Other co-sharers Annada Charan Saha, Kanjiram Saha, Jotnamoyee Saha, Narayan Chandra' Saha and Hare Krishan Saha also sold out 0.94 acre of land from the aforesaid plots as described in the schedule to the plaint to the plaintiff-respondents-Abul Kashem Bepari, the father of defendant Nos. 1-7 and husband of the defendant No. 8 vide deed No. 4992 dated 7-7-1985 pursuant to which the plaintiff got 0.63 acre of land in 2/3 rd share and the said Abul Kashem Bepari died leaving behind defendants No. 1-8 who inherited the said 0.31 acre of land. The plaintiff-respondent No. 1 sold out 0.25 1/3 acre of land out of 0.31 acre, which he got vide deed No. 4992 dated 7-7-1985 to the defendant No. 8 (mother of defendant Nos. 1-7) vide deed No. 1325 dated 19-9-1990 and, as such, defendant Nos. 1-8 became owners of 0.31+25 1/3 = 0.56 1/3 acre of land and the plaintiffs-respondents became owners of 1.64½ decimal of land. Under these circumstances defendant Nos. 1-8 filed Title Suit No. 6 of 2003 for declaration of title and confirmation of possession over 0.72½ acre of land, as described in the schedule `Kha' to the plaint. In the said suit, Harihar Biswas, the defendant-petitioner No. 9 was made defendant No. 1 and Chandra Kanta Saha and Lalit Mohan Saha two dead persons were made defendants Nos. 2 and 3 respectively without impleading the present plaintiff-respondent as party in the suit who are in possession of the suit land being its lawful owners and thereby obtained a collusive sole decree (compromise decree) on 27-5-2003. When on the basis of such collusive decree they threatened the plaintiff respondents on 2-6-2003 to evict them from the suit land, then the plaintiff came to know about the said collusive and illegal decree which is not binding upon the plaintiffs. Hence, they filed the suit.
3. Defendants Nos. 1, 3, 7 and 8 contested the suit by filing written statement, contending, inter alia, that the suit is barred by limitation and for mis-joinder and non joinder of parties. The suit land, appertaining to Mouza Amtali, RS Khatian No. 40 measuring 1.01 acre was owned and possessed admittedly by Annada Chandra Saha and his co-sharers in their respective shares within the same Mouza, another 1.01acre land appertaining to RS Khatian No. 27 was also owned and possessed by the above noted persons in their respective shares. The said Sahas owned and possessed 0.44 acre of land in Unisa Mouza appertaining to RS Khatian No. 155 in their respective shares. On 15 Poush, 1357 BS Chandra Kanto Saha and Lalit Mohon Saha gave 0.72½ acre of land in favour of Abul Kashem Bepari, the father of defendant Nos. 1-7 as Rayati settlement on which the said Abul Kashem erected his house, planted trees and was living peacefully before he died leaving behind defendant Nos. 1-7 as his sons and daughters and defendant No. 8, his wife as heirs. As one Harihar BiswaS and others threatened them to disposes from the said land the defendant Nos. 1-8 filed Title Suit No. 6 of 2003 against the said Harihar Biswas, Chandra Kanto and Lalit Mohan Saha as defendants wherein summons were issued upon them. Since Chandra Kanto Saha and Lalit Mohan Saha had no interest in the suit land they did not appear before the court in the said suit but Harihar Biswas appeared and upon admitting the right, title and interest of defendant Nos. 1-8 over the suit land executed a solenama in their favour, on the basis of which the suit was decreed in terms of the solenama. Hence, the present defendants were owning and possessing the said 0.72½ acre of land for over 12 years. Late Abul Kashem Bepari purchased 0.25 acre of land from one Usha Rani, vide deed No. 964 dated 16-9-1972 and defendant No. 8 Ayesha Bibi purchased 0.25 acre of land from plaintiff No. 1 vide deed No. 2324 dated 19-9-1990. Chandra Kanto Saha and Lalit Mohon Saha sold 0.95 acre of land to the plaintiffs and late Abul Kashem Bepari from RS Khatian Nos. 27, 40 and 155 out of which the share of Abul Kashem Bepari has been inherited by defendant Nos. 1-8 and, as such, the defendants are owning and possessing 1.54¼ acre of land for a period of 12 years. The plaintiffs Irive no possession in the suit land and they have filed the suit with false and concocted story of purchase on the basis of a forged deed dated 16-8-1982. Hence, the suit is liable to be dismissed.
4. At the trial, respective parties adduced evidence both oral and documentary in support of their respective case. The trial Court decreed the suit by its judgment and decree dated 6-7-2006, against which defendants Nos. 3, 7 and 8 preferred Title Appeal No. 59 of 2006 before the District Judge, Gopalgonj and the same was ultimately heard by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gopalgonj, who by his judgment and decree dated 30-3-2010 allowed the appeal.
5. The plaintiffs-respondents then moved before the High Court Division by filing Civil Revision No. 3441 of 2010 and obtained Rule. Upon hearing, a single Bench of the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and order made the Rule absolute.
6. Being aggrieved by the said judgment and order the defendants as petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 1553 of 2017 before this Division and, accordingly, leave was granted on 1-4-2019. Hence, this appeal.
7. Mr M Quamrul Haque Siddique, the learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the appellants submits that the High Court Division has erred in law in reversing the judgment and decree, passed by the appellate Court without adverting to the findings of the appellate Court that Chandra Kanta Saha and Lolit Mohon Saha had in total 0.72½ acre of land in their share of RS Khatian Nos. 27, 40 and 155, which were acquired by Abul Kashem Bepari by pattan.
8. The learned Advocate also submits that the High Court Division erred in making the Rule absolute holding that the appellate Court had failed to comply with the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
9. Per contra Mr Probir Neogi, learned Senior Advocate, appearing for the respondents made submissions in support of the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division. Mr Neogi also submits that the High Court Division while exercising its revisional jurisdiction is competent to reverse the judgment of the Courts below, since the same has been made upon misreading and non-consideration of the material evidence causing failure of justice, as a matter of course, judgment passed by the High Court Division having been in true spirit of laws and principles in exercise of discretionary civil revisional power to do complete justice between the litigant parties for the administration of which also it had been created and the same having been well founded, well grounded and well-reasoned and no illegality and legal infirmity having been manifested, no interference is called for by this Division. The learned Advocate further submits that the appellate Court without proper appreciation of the evidence on record and without adverting the findings of the trial Court with regard to title and possession, perfunctorily reversed the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court, inasmuch as the rayati settlement (pattan) in favour of the predecessor of the defendants was not substantiated before the trial Court; despite, mere submitting a rent receipt is not sufficient to prove their right and title in the suit land.
10. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates for the parties concerned, perused the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division as well as the Courts below and other connected papers on record.
11. In the instant case the Court of Appeal below set-aside the decree passed in favour of the plaintiff holding that the plaintiff's suit without prayer of declaration of title is not maintainable. The Court of Appeal below, being the final Court of fact upon consideration of the evidence of record further held to the effect: —
"বাদীদের দাবীকৃত অংশ, বাবদ বাদীগন স্বত্ব ঘোষনা পূর্বক বাটোয়ারা দাবী না করায় উক্ত ছোলে ডিক্রি অবৈধ বে- আইনী ঘোষনা আদৌ আইন সঙ্গত না হওয়ায় উক্ত রায় ও ডিক্রী বহাল থাকিতে পারে না।"
12. Upon perusal of the plaint, it transpires that the plaintiffs filed the suit only for declaration that the sole decree (compromise decree) dated 27-5-2003 and decree signed on 1-6-2003 is collusive, null and void and not binding upon the plaintiffs. The said sole decree was passed in respect of 72½ decimals land described in schedule `Kha' to the plaint. The plaintiffs claim title in respect of 2.21 acres land described in schedule 'Ka' which appertaining in different khatians and 4 (four) plots.
13. If we consider the plaint and prayer of the plaintiffs, it is abundantly clear that the land described in `kha' schedule, which was the issue in sole decree is not identifiable and from the evidence, it shows that both the plaintiffs and defendants have been possessing the said land.
14. In view of the above, we are of the opinion that the trial Court as well as the High Court Division committed error in decreeing the suit and, as such, the impugned judgment is liable to be interfered.
<u><u>15. The High Court Division set-aside the judgment and decree of the Court of appeal below holding that the appellate Court without reversing the findings of the trial Court with reference to the evidence on record passed the judgment, and the High Court Division also observed that the appellant without complying the provision of Order XLI, rule 31 of the Code of Civil Procedure passed the judgment and decree. Upon perusal of the judgment of the Court of appeal below it transpires that the Court of appeal below being final court of fact addressed and settled all the issues involved in the suit with reference to the evidence on record. Thus, the findings and observations of the High Court Division is not proper, and illegal. Thus, the impugned judgment is required to be interfered.</u></u>
16. Accordingly, the appeal is disposed of.
17. The judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is set-aside.
18. However, the plaintiffs are at liberty to file appropriate suit in appropriate forum for their redress, if so advised.
No order as to costs.
End.

full_judgment:
SM Maniruzzaman, J: In this Rule nisi, the respondents have been called upon to show cause as to why the order dated 6-10-2019 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat Number 2, Dhaka in Miscellaneous Case Number 30 of 2019 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit Number 502 of 2017) rejecting the same should not be declared to have been passed without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and or such other or further order or orders should not be passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. At the time of issuance of the Rule, the operation of the judgment and decree dated 30-6-2009 passed in the original suit was stayed.
2. Facts, for disposal of the Rule, are that the petitioner is a businessman and for expansion of his business obtained loan amounting to Taka 8,00,000 (eight lac) from the BRAC Bank Limited, Head Office, Dhaka. As, the petitioner failed to re-pay the loan, the creditor-bank instituted Artha Rin Suit Number 502 of 2017 in the Artha Rin Adalat Number 2, Dhaka which was decreed ex-parte on 30-6-2019 (decree signed on 7-7-2019). The petitioner after knowing about the ex-parte decree filed Miscellaneous Case Number 30 of 2019 under Section 19(2) of Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (in short, the Ain) for setting aside the ex-park judgment and decree by depositing 10% of the decretal amount that came to Taka 1,51,629.20 through a pay order.
3. After hearing the petitioner, the Artha Rin Adalat summarily rejected the miscellaneous case by its order dated 6-10-2019. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the said order, the petitioner moved with this application and obtained the Rule.
4. The petitioner by filing a supplementary affidavit further stated that during pendency of the Rule, the loan in question has already been re-scheduled by the bank and as per terms of the re-schedulment, the petitioner deposited Taka 5,06,630 and rest amount of Taka 1,51,629.20 will be paid after disposal of the Case.
5. Mr Khandakar Ahsan Habib, learned Advocate submits that the petitioner as a bonafide business man has no intention to avoid the payment of loan but due to pandemic situation he was quite unable to pay the loan within the stipulated time. The petitioner duly appointed his advocate to conduct the suit, but due to negligence of the learned advocate, the artha rin suit was disposed of ex-parte. As soon as the petitioner came to know about the ex-parte decree, he filed the miscellaneous case by depositing 10% of decreetal amount, but learned Judge of the Artha Rin Adalat without considering the fact summarily rejected the miscellaneous case by the impugned order. Mr Habib next submits that since the loan in question has already been re-scheduled by the bank and for disposal of the suit in terms of solanama, the impugned order is to be set-aside for the ends of justice.
6. Mr Chowdhury Mokimuddin KJ Ali, learned Advocate for the respondent-bank accepts the submission of learned Advocate for the petitioner and affirms that the loan in question has already been re-scheduled by the bank by letter dated 26-2-2003 and as per terms of the re-schedulement, the petitioner has already paid Taka 4,05,000 (four lac five thousand) and the rest amount of Taka 1,51,630 will be paid after disposal of the case. In view of the said fact he prays for passing necessary order for the ends of justice.
7. We have considered the submissions of the learned Advocates of both the sides, gone through the writ petition, supplementary affidavits to the writ petition and materials on record appended thereto. It appears from record that the petitioner instituted Miscellaneous Case Number 30 of 2019 under Section 19(2) of the Ain, 2003 for setting aside the ex-parte decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat on 30-9-2019. The petitioner categorically stated that the ex-parte decree came to his knowledge on 22-8-2019 and finally he was confirmed about the date of ex-parte decree on 25-8-2019 from the learned Advocate of the trial Court. Thereafter, he instituted the miscellaneous case on 29-8-2019 within 30 (thirty) days from the date of his knowledge. It also appears that the petitioner has deposited 10% of the decretal amount at the time of filing of the miscellaneous case.
<u>8. Section 19 (2) of the Ain provides that if any suit is decreed ex-parte, the defendant may within 30 (thirty) days from the dated of such ex-parte decree or his knowledge about such ex-parte decree subject to provision of Sub section 3 file a prayer for cancellation of such ex-parte decree. Sub section (3) provides that the defendant shall be required to deposit 10% of the decreetal amount with the application under section 19 (2) of the Ain.</u>
9. It thus appears that the petitioner instituted the miscellaneous case within 30 (thirty) days from the date of his knowledge of the ex-parte decree by fulfillment of the requirement as provided in section 19 (3) of the Ain, but the learned Judge of the the Artha Rin Adalat without applying his judicial mind and without considering the relevant facts summarily rejected the miscellaneous case by the impugned order and thereby committed an error.
10. It further appears from the supplementary affidavit filed by the petitioner that during pendency of the Rule, the loan has already been re-scheduled by the bank. As per terms of the re-schedulement, the petitioner has deposited Taka 4,05,000 (four lac five thousand) and the remaining amount of loan will be adjusted after settlement of the case.
11. In view of the stated circumstances, we find substance in the submission made by the learned advocate for the petitioner and merit in the Rule.
Accordingly, the Rule is made absolute, however, without any order as to costs. The impugned order dated 6-10-2019 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat Number 2, Dhaka rejecting Miscellaneous Case Number 30 of 2019 (arising out of Artha Rin Suit Number 502 of 2017) is hereby declared to have been passed without lawful authority and of no legal effect. The Artha Rin Suit Number 502 of 2017 is restored in its original file and number.
End.

full_judgment:
This Rule was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the judgment and order dated 16-9-2020 passed by the Additional District Judge, First Court, Tangail in Civil Revision No. 28 of 2014 rejecting the revisional application and thereby affirming the judgment and order dated 2-6-2014 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail in Miscellaneous Case No. 72 of 2004 allowing the application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure and set-aside the preliminary decree dated 12-8-2002 and final decree dated 28-4-2003 passed in Title Suit No.251 of 1994 should not be set-aside and such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper.
2. The facts, relevant for the disposal of the Rule, in brief, is that the predecessors of the petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No.14 of 1982 in the Court of the then Sub-ordinate Judge, Second Court, Tangail for partition of land described in the schedules to the plaint, praying for their saham of 5.62½ decline's of land out of 26.66 decirnels. Subsequently, the suit was transferred to the court of the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail and renumbered as Title Suit No. 251 of 1994. The suit was ready for hearing but none of the defendants appeared before the Court. So, the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail decreed the suit ex-parte in preliminary form on 12-8-2002. Thereafter the plaintiff filed Decree Execution case No. 9 of 2003 and the final ex-parte decree was delivered on 28-4-2003. The defendant Nos. 140, 156 and 157 of the partition suit came to know about the ex-parte decree on 9-8-2004 and filed Miscellaneous Case No. 72 of 2004 on 25-8-2004 before the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure praying for setting aside the preliminary and final ex-parte decree dated 12-8-2002 and 28.4-2003 respectively passed in Title Suit No. 251 of 1994 alleging inter aria that the summons of the suit was not served upon them. They were not aware of the judgment and decree. The plaintiffs as opposite party Nos. 1, 3 and 4 contested the Miscellaneous Case by filing a written objection stating that the petitioners-defendants were aware of the judgment and decree and they received the summons through his full brother, but they did not contest the suit. The Senior Assistant judge, Sadar Court, Tangail framed as many as two issues for the determination of the dispute between the parties. The petitioners examined as many as three witnesses and opposite parties also examined three witnesses to prove their respective cases- Upon hearing both the parties, considering the evidence on record the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail allowed the Miscellaneous Case on 2-6-2014.
3. Challenging the impugned judgment and order passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail in Miscellaneous Case No.72 of 2004, the plaintiffs as petitioners preferred Civil Revision No. 28 of 2014 before the District Judge, Tangail. Subsequently, the Civil Revision was transferred. to the Additional District Judge, First Court, Tangail. Upon hearing the parties the Additional District Judge, First Court, Tangail rejected the Civil Revision and upheld the order dated 2-6-2014 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail in Miscellaneous Case No. 72 of 2004.
4. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the judgment and order passed by the learned Additional District Judge, First Court, Tangail, the plaintiffs as petitioners filed the instant revisional application before this Court and upon hearing this Court granted leave and issued this Rule.
5. Mr Md Shahidul Islam, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that the defendants as petitioners filed Miscellaneous Case No. 72 of 2004 to harass the plaintiffs though they have no right, title or interest in the suit land. He further submits that the summons was duly served upon the defendants following the provision of Order V, rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure. He next submits that it is clearly mentioned in the Limitation Act that under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure, a Miscellaneous case is to be filed within 30 days from the date of ex-parte decree or date of knowledge. ex-parte decree was passed on 12-8-2002 and final decree was passed on 28-4-2003 and the opposite parties got knowledge about the ex-parte decree on 20-7-2004 from Abdur Rashid (Pt.W-2) but the Miscellaneous case was filed on 25-8-2004 that is after 05 days out of time and thus the Miscellaneous Case was barred by limitation.
6. On the other hand, Mr Mohammad Ali, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the opposite parties submits that Md Sekandar Ali was defendant No.140, SM Jahid Alam alias Pintu Miah was defendant No. 157 and Mosammat farina Khatun was defendant No.156. The summons was not served upon them. The process server (OPW-2) served the summons of the defendant Nos.140, 156 and 157 on SM Shafikul Islam. The said defendants did not reside in a common house with SM Shafikul Islam at the time of serving of summons. SM Shafikul Islam was not authorized agent to receive the summons. Since the summons was not duly served upon the defendant Nos. 140, 156 and 157 there is no illegality in the order dated 2-6-2014 passed by the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail in Miscellaneous case No.72 of 2004 as well as in the judgment and order dated 16-9-2020 passed by the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Tangail.
7. He further submits that Shafikul Islam is a vital witness but he was not examined by the plaintiffs-opposite parties-petitioners.
8. Heard the learned Advocates for both sides, perused the Civil Revision, judgment and order and other materials on record.
9. P.W 1, Md Sikander Ali stated in his deposition,
"২৫১/৯৪ নং বাটোয়ারা মোকদ্দমায় আমাদের নামীয় সমন আমার ছোট ভাই এ.এস.এম শফিকুল আলম স্বাক্ষর দিয়া রাখে, আমাদের উপর সমন সঠিক ভাবে জারী করা হয় নাই। আমার ছোট ভাই এ.এস.এম শফিকুল আলমের সহিত দীর্ঘ দিন যাবত আমার শত্রুতা আছে। ইং ২০-৭-২০০৪ তারিখ সকাল অনুমান ৮-০০ টার সময় আসিয়া আমার বর্গাদার আব্দুর রশিদ আমার বাসায় আসিয়া জানান যে, আমাদের স্বত্ব দখলীয় সম্পত্তিতে প্রতিপক্ষ ইনুছ আলী জমির দখল নিবে বলিয়া প্রকাশ করিয়াছে। অতঃপর ২২-৭-২০০৪ ইং তারিখে আমি আদালতে আসিয়া তালাস অনুসন্ধান করিয়া ৯-৮-২০০৪ ইং তারিখে রায় ও ডিক্রির জাবেদা নকল প্রাপ্ত হইয়া রায় ও ডিক্রি সম্পর্কে অবগত হই। আমি উক্ত ২৫১/৯৪ নং বাটোয়ারা মোকদ্দমা সম্পর্কে ইতোপূর্বে জানিতে পারি নাই। উক্ত ২৫১/৯৪ নং বাটোয়ারা মোকদ্দমার বাদীপক্ষ আমার বাসস্থানের ঠিকানা জানিত কিন্তু তাহা সত্বেও আমার বাসস্থানের ঠিকানায় সমন জারী না করিয়া আমার পৈত্রিক বাড়ীর ঠিকানায় আমাদের অজ্ঞাতে অসাক্ষাতে আমার ছোট ভাইয়ের মাধ্যমে সমন জারীর কথা উল্লেখ করিয়াছেন। আমাদের উপর সমন জারী করা হইলে আমরা উক্ত ২৫১/৯৪ নং বাটোয়ারা মোকদ্দমায় প্রতিদ্বন্দ্বিতা করিতাম।"
10. OPW-2, Abul Kashem, the process server in his deposition stated that—
বাটোয়ারা মোকদ্দমার বিবাদী সেকান্দার আলীর নাম ১৪০ নং বিবাদী হিসেবে উল্লেখ আছে। ১৫৭ নং বিবাদী হিসেবে এস.এম. জাহিদ আলম, ১৫৬ নং বিবাদী হিসেবে মোছাঃ জরিনা খাতুনের নাম উল্লেখ আছে। তারা এ মামলার ১-৩ নং প্রার্থী। ১৪০ ও ১৫৭ নং বিবাদীর যথাক্রমে ভাই ও চাচা সমন গ্রহণ করেন। ১৪১ নং বিবাদী সেকান্দারের ভাই। ১৫৬ নং বিবাদীর সমন তার দেবর ১৪১ নং বিবাদী গ্রহণ করেন। এইভাবে আমি জারী করি। সে সমনে জারী কারক হিসেবে আমার সই আছে। In cross-examination the process server deposed that ১৪০, ১৫৬ ও ১৫৭ নং বিবাদীর উপর সমন ব্যক্তিগতভাবে জারী করিনি। ১৪১ নং বিবাদী শফিকুলের কাছে দিয়া আসি। আমি জিজ্ঞাসা করলে বাড়িতে নাই বলে।
11. OPW-1, kid Abdul Gani in cross-examination admitted that—
সত্য যে তাদের নামে ব্যক্তিগতভাবে নোটিশ পায়নি। প্রার্থীর ভাই পায়। প্রার্থীর ভাই শফিকুলকে সাক্ষী হিসেবে আনিনি।
12. It is divulged from the above mentioned evidence that although SM Shafiqul Islam is a brother of Sikandar Ali, they resided separately. They were not living in a common house when receiving the summons. It transpires that there was enmity between Sikandar Ali and SM Shafiqul Islam. So, it is apparent that SM Shafiqul Islam was not an authorized agent empowered to accept service of the summons on behalf of defendants No. 140, 156 and 157 with any document showing such authorization under Order 3 Rule 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure. OPW-2, the process server admitted in his evidence that he served the summons of defendants. No.140, 156 and 157 on SM Shafiqul Islam. Hence, it is evident that the service of summons to SM Shafiqul Islam was not a due service to bind the defendants. Thus, the plaintiffs-petitioners failed to prove that summonses were duly served upon Sikandar Ali (defendant No.140), SM Jahid Alam alias Pintu Miah (defendant No.157) and Mosammat Jarina Khatun (defendant No.156). Since it has been found that the provision contained in Order V, rule 15 of the Code of Civil Procedure has no application to the facts and circumstances of the case, no relief can be claimed by the plaintiff-opposite parties-petitioners relying on that provision. In Osir Uddin Mandal and others vs Azizur Rahman, reported in 39 DLR 403, this Court observed that law in this regard enjoins that service of summons on the defendant is to be proved strictly according to law and, if proof is lacking in this regard, mercy or plea of ends of justice cannot come in rescue of the aggrieved party.
13. Having considered materials on record, facts, circumstances and legal and factual aspects of the matter, I am of the opinion that the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail and the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Tangail rightly held that service of summons was not duly served upon the defendants in accordance with law and hence, they legally set-aside the ex-parte decree following the provisions of Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure.
14. I get strong support from the decision passed in Abdur Rashid and another vs Abdul Barik and another, reported in 35 DLR (AD) (1983) 162, the Apex Court held:
"Under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code, if the summons is not duly served on the defendant, that is a good ground for setting aside on ex-parte decree. On a perusal of the relevant provisions of the Code of Civil Procedure it would be apparent, that the due service of summons is an essential condition, which must be satisfied before the court can proceed to give a judgment and order under Order IX, rule 13 if a party satisfies a Court that summons were not duly served upon him, the Court is bound to set-aside an ex-parte decree. In such a case, question of knowledge is not at all relevant and an ex-parte decree will be set-aside even if the defendant had knowledge of the institution of a suit."
15. It appears from the evidence of P.W 1, Md Sikandar Ali that bargadar Abdur Rashid communicated to him on 20-7-2004 that Innash All had got a decree and he would take possession of the suit land. Pt.W-2, Abdur Rashid corroborated the evidence adduced by Pt.W-1. Upon receipt of the information the defendant-petitioner-opposite parties went to the Court on 22-7-2004 and obtained the certified copy on 9-8-2004 and filed the application under Order IX, ntle 13 on 25-8-2004.
16. It is evident that the defendant got definite knowledge of the ex-parte decree on 9-8-2004 after obtaining certified copy, thereafter he filed the Miscellaneous Case on 25-8-2004 under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure within 30 days from the date of knowledge of the ex-parte decree as per provision of Article 164 of the Limitation Act. To appreciate this point it would be better if the said Article is quoted below. It runs as follows:-
Description of suit
Period of limitation
Time from which period begins to run.
164. By a defendant, for an order to set-aside a decree passed ex-parte.
Thirty days
The date of the decree or, where the summons was not duly served, when the applicant has knowledge of the decree.
<u>17. It is evident that, Article 164 of the Limitation Act provides that if the summons is not served then limitation will run from the date of knowledge.</u>
<u>18. My considered view is that the Miscellaneous case under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure was filed within 30 days of the date of knowledge and the same is not barred by limitation. Considering this aspect of the matter I am unable to accept the contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner. 19. In my view, the Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail has rightly and legally arrived at the finding that the service of summons could not be proved by the plaintiffs to maintain the ex-parte decree and the Additional District Judge, 1st Court, Tangail rightly rejected the civil revision affirming the judgment and order dated 2-6-2014 passed in Miscellaneous case No. 72 of 2004.</u>
20. 1 find no merit and substance in the instant Civil Revision.
21. So, the Rule is discharged.
22. There is no order as to costs.
23. Title suit No. 251 of 1994, pending in the learned Senior Assistant Judge, Sadar Court, Tangail is hereby restored to its file and number setting aside the ex-parte decree to decide the dispute on merit which can only meet the real justice. The Court is also directed to dispose of the suit expeditiously.
Let a copy of the judgment and order along with Lower Court Records be transmitted to the Court concerned forthwith.
End.

case_source: (From the judgment and decree dated 18-5-2009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No. 271 of 1998)
full_judgment:
Hasan Foez Siddique, CJ: This civil appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 18-5-20009 passed by the High Court Division in First Appeal No.271 of 1998 reversing those dated 29-6-1998 passed by the learned Joint District Judge, First Court, Feni in Title Suit No. 12 of 1997.
2. The facts, relating to the appeal, in a nutshell, are that the plaintiff-respondent filed Title Suit No.12 of 1997 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Feni for declaration that the ex-parte decree dated 28-1-1997 in Title Suit No.5 of 1996 was fraudulent and void. Appellant Din Mohammad instituted aforesaid suit against the respondent Mafizur Rahman Mia for a decree of specific performance of contract. No process was served upon this plaintiff. Defendant obtained an ex-parte decree on 18-1-1997 by suppressing the summons. The plaintiff came to know about the ex-parte decree and kabala deed (through Court) from one Joynul Abedin on 8-6-1997. He was an accused of GR No.464 of 1995 and defendant petitioner No.1, who was his neighbor, assured him to take necessary tadbir for him in the said GR case. Thereafter, in collusion with his (defendant-petitioner) maternal cousin Nasir, who was a Mohrar in Criminal Court, he obtained his signatures on vokalatnama and a stamp paper worth of Taka 50 on the plea of swearing affidavit and also on different cartridge papers etc. giving him assurance to get release from custody on bail. Thereafter, it transpired that by manipulating respondent's signatures obtained thereon, the appellant prepared a bainapatra and a vokalatnama. A written statement was also shown to have been submitted by the respondent in Title Suit No. 5 of 1996 admitting the claim. The said bainapatra was fabricated and was not executed by the respondent nor did he submit any written statement. Under the aforesaid circumstances, the plaintiff respondent instituted the instant Title Suit for setting aside the ex-park decree passed in Title Suit No.05 of 1996, which was allegedly obtained against him by suppression of summons and by producing fictitious bainapatra etc.
3. Defendant appellant No.1 contested the suit by filing, written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint. His case was that the plaintiff respondent entered into an agreement to sell the suit land to him for a consideration of Taka 2,00,000. Out of which, he received a sum of Taka 18,000 and executed a "bainapatra" in favour of the appellant on 17-4-1996. The plaintiff respondent having refused to execute and register the deed, he instituted Title Suit No.5 of 1996 for specific performance of contract and all the processes were duly issued and served upon the plaintiff respondent who appeared in the suit by filing a vokalatnama and submitted a written statement. But ultimately, he did not contest the suit. As a result, judgment and decree was passed in favour of the defendant appellant. The suit is liable to be dismissed.
4. The trial Court dismissed the suit. The plaintiff preferred First Appeal in the High court Division and the High Court Division by the impugned judgment and decree allowed appeal upon setting aside the judgment and decree of the trial Court. Thus, defendant No.1 has preferred this appeal upon getting leave.
5. Mr Raziuddin Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the appellant, submits that the instant suit was hopelessly barred by limitation and in order to get rid of a point of limitation, the plaintiff has made some false assertion, in such view of the matter, the judgment and decree of the High Court Division is liable to be seaside. He further submits that the trial Court brought the lower Courts record of Title Suit No.5 of 1996 and examined the process server who categorically deposed that the respondent No.1 was not willing to receive the summons of the case for which the process server served the summon by way of hanging with the outer door of the respondent. He, lastly, submits that the High Court Division without appreciation of the evidence on record, erroneously reversed the well reasoned judgment and decree of the trial Court.
6. Mr Khair Ezaz Maswood, learned Senior Advocate appearing for the respondent, submits that the High Court Division upon proper appreciation of the evidence on record found that the defendant No.1 obtained ex-parte decree by practising fraud upon the Court and that the notice of Title Suit No. 5 of 1996 was not duly served upon the defendant No.1 (plaintiff of this suit) and that it rightly reversed the judgment and decree of the trial Court.
<u><u>7. The plea of the plaintiff respondent was that the appellant obtained ex-parte decree by practising fraud so the same is a nullity but in a given case whether such decree was obtained by fraud or not, is a matter which is to be judged with reference to pleadings and evidence on record. The Courts of law are meant for imparting justice between the parties. No Court can be regarded as powerless to recall its own order if it is convinced that order was wangled through fraud or misrepresentation of such a dimension as would affect the very basis of the claim. It appears from the materials on record that earlier the appellant instituted Title Suit No.5 of 1996 for specific performance of contract on 6-6-1996. The trial Court directed to issue process through the Process server as well as by registered post and fixed 7-7-1996 for return. It further appears from the judgment of the High Court Division that it considered the evidence both oral and documentary came to conclusion that notice upon the defendant of Title Suit No. 5 of 1996, that is, the plaintiff of present suit, was not duly served and decree had been obtained by fraudulent suppression of the summons upon the defendant No.1 of the said suit.</u></u>
8. Since the last Court of facts upon proper appreciation of the evidence of record held that notice upon the defendant No.1 of the said suit was not duly served and plaintiff of the said suit obtained decree by practising fraud upon the Court, we are of the view, that it rightly set-aside the ex-parte decree and directed the trial Court to allow the defendant of the said suit to file written statement upon restoring the Title Suit No.5 of 1996 to its original file and number.
9. Accordingly, we do not find any substance in the appeal.
Thus, the appeal is dismissed.
End.
